question.text: Consider the system of linear equations \[ \begin{cases} x_1 - x_2 + 2x_3= 2\\ x_1 - 3x_3 = 1. \end{cases} \] Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.explanation:
The augmented matrix for this system is
\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 & 1 \end{array} \right]. \]

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

\[\begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1& -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 & 1 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:=R_2-R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -1 \\ \end{array}\right]& R_1 &:=R_1 + R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -1 \\ \end{array}\right] \end{align*}\]

The corresponding system is now

\[ \left\{ \begin{align*} &x_1-3x_3 = 1\\ &x_2-5x_3= -1.\\ \end{align*} \right. \]

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x_1$ and $x_2,$ and we have one free variable, $x_3.$ That means we need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ in terms of $x_3.$

Therefore, the general solution is

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x_1= 3x_3+1 \\ x_2= 5x_3-1 \\ x_3= x_3, \end{array} \right. \]

where $x_3$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

\begin{align*} \begin{bmatrix}x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 3x_3+1 \\ 5x_3-1 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad x_3 \in (-\infty,\infty). \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the system of linear equations \[ \begin{cases} x_1 + 3x_2 + x_3= -1\\ -2x_1 - 5x_2 = 3. \end{cases} \] Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

The augmented matrix for this system is
\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & -5 & 0 & 3 \end{array} \right]. \]

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

\[\begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1& 3 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & -5 & 0 & 3 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:=R_2+2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ \end{array}\right]& R_1 &:=R_1 - 3R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -5 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ \end{array}\right] \end{align*}\]

The corresponding system is now

\[ \left\{ \begin{align*} &x_1-5x_3 = -4\\ &x_2+2x_3= 1.\\ \end{align*} \right. \]

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x_1$ and $x_2,$ and we have one free variable, $x_3.$ That means we need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ in terms of $x_3.$

Therefore, the general solution is

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x_1= 5x_3-4 \\ x_2= 1-2x_3 \\ x_3= x_3, \end{array} \right. \]

where $x_3$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

\begin{align*} \begin{bmatrix}x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 5x_3-4 \\ 1-2x_3 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad x_3 \in (-\infty,\infty). \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the system of linear equations \[ \left\{ \begin{align*} &x -2y +2z =2\\ &y-z = -1. \end{align*} \right. \] Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

The augmented matrix for this system is \[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \end{array} \right]. \]

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

\[\begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \end{array}\right]& R_1 &:= R_1 + 2R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}\]

The corresponding system is now
\[ \left\{ \begin{align*} & x=0\\ & y-z = -1. \end{align*} \right. \] The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$

Therefore, the general solution is

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x=0 \\ y=z -1\\ z= z, \end{array} \right. \]

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as \begin{align*} \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ z-1 \\ z \end{bmatrix}, \qquad z \in (-\infty,\infty). \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the system of linear equations \[ \left\{ \begin{align*} &-x + 2y = -1 \\ &4x - 8y = 4 \\ &-4x + 8y = -4. \end{align*} \right. \] Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.explanation:
The augmented matrix for this system is
\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & -8 & 4 \\ -4 & 8 & -4 \end{array} \right]. \]

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

\[\begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & -8 & 4 \\ -4 & 8 & -4 \end{array}\right] & R_1 &:= -R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 4 & -8 & 4 \\ -4 & 8 & -4 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 - 4R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 8 & -4 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:=R_3 + 4R_1\\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}\]

The corresponding system is now

\[ \left\{ \begin{align*} &x - 2y = 1 \\ \end{align*} \right. \]

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y.$

Therefore, the general solution is

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x= 2y+1 \\ y=y, \end{array} \right. \]

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

\begin{align*} \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2y+1 \\ y \end{bmatrix}, \qquad y \in (-\infty,\infty). \end{align*}

question.text:
Consider the following system of equations. \[ \left\{ \begin{align*} &-x +y= -1\\ &2x+3y =3\\ &-x-4y=-3. \end{align*} \right. \] Which of the following statements are true?

  1. The system is inconsistent
  2. The system has a unique solution
  3. The system is consistent dependent
question.explanation:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is \[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 & 3 \\ -1 & -4 & -3 \end{array} \right]. \] Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

\[\begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 & 3 \\ -1 & -4 & -3 \end{array}\right]& R_2 &:= R_2+2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 \\ -1 & -4 & -3 \end{array}\right]& R_3 &:= R_3+(-1)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & -2 \end{array}\right]& R_3 &:= R_3+R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}\]

The final row corresponds to the equation $0x+0y=-1,$ and this has no solution. Therefore, our system has no solution, and we conclude that the system is inconsistent.

As a result, only statement I is true.

The final row corresponds to the equation $0x+0y=-150,$ and this has no solution. Therefore, our system has no solution, and we conclude that the system is inconsistent.

question.text: Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is consistent dependent: \[ \begin{cases} x +2y =3\\ -3x-(k+1)y = -9 \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
The augmented matrix for this system is \[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -3 \\ -3 & -(k+1) & -9 \end{array} \right]. \]

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

\[\begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ - 3 & -(k+1) &- 9 \end{array}\right]& R_2 &:=R_2 + 3R_1\\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -k+5 &0 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}\]

The corresponding system is now

\[ \begin{cases} 1 -2y =3\\ -(k-5)y = 0. \end{cases} \] The system is consistent dependent if it has infinitely many solutions. For the system to have infinitely many solutions, it must have at least one free variable.

If $k=5,$ then the second equation is $0=0,$ which is true for any value of $y$, and we can remove this equation from the system. As a result, the system will contain only one equation, $x +2y = 3.$

Then, the basic variable will be $x,$ and we will have a free variable $y.$ That means the system will have infinitely many solutions.

Therefore, our system is consistent dependent when $k=5.$
